title: Bram and the Confession
premise: When a stranger's corpse is found on the marsh road wearing clothes stolen from retired detective Emrys Ishikawa's own bookshop stockroom, the town of Hollowmere assumes it's a cruel prank — until Emrys recognizes the dead man as the brother of a witness who vanished seven years ago, the night his last case went cold. Following a ledger disguised as his late wife's recipe book, Emrys uncovers that the town's founding families have been quietly paying for silence about a drowning they all witnessed. The killer is the one person who has been protecting Emrys all along: his lodger and surrogate daughter, Wren, who killed to stop her father's confession from destroying the family that took her in. In the end, Emrys must choose between turning her in and burning the ledger — and he chooses a third path, confessing to his own seven years of complicity so that Wren can finally be free.
about_author: Casper Eriksen is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent a decade shelving mysteries before writing one. They live near the coast with two opinionated cats and an ever-growing stack of unread first editions.

chapters.title: The Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. A foggy October morning brings Police Sergeant Hale to the bookshop: a man found dead on the marsh road, dressed head to toe in garments from Emrys's own stockroom. Emrys recognizes the coat immediately — he sold it to a frightened visitor three nights ago. The beat is dread wrapped in quiet competence; Emrys's detective instincts wake after seven years asleep.

chapters.title: A Ledger of Recipes and Lies
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Sorting the victim's effects, Emrys finds a handwritten recipe book tucked inside the stolen coat — but the 'recipes' are coded entries: dates, initials, sums of money. He recognizes his late wife Marian's handwriting style and realizes the book was copied from something she once owned. Emotional beat: grief rekindled, suspicion turned inward toward his own household.

chapters.title: Wren Knows Too Much
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Emrys's young lodger watches him decode the ledger at night and quietly moves pieces against him — returning a borrowed key, deflecting Hale's questions. Through her eyes we see she loves Emrys like a father and is terrified of what the ledger will make him do. The beat is tenderness laced with guilt; readers sense she's hiding something without knowing what.

chapters.title: The Drowning at Ferrow Mill
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The decoded entries point to 1998 and a boy who drowned at the old mill — officially an accident, actually witnessed by four founding-family children who swore a pact of silence. One witness was Wren's father, Daniel Voss, who disappeared from Hollowmere seven years ago. Beat: revelation; Emrys realizes his coldest case and this murder share a root.

chapters.title: What the Founding Families Paid For
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys confronts the surviving witnesses — now the town's doctor, bank manager, and churchwarden — and finds them old, frightened, and still paying into a fund administered through Marian's estate. His wife knew. The emotional beat is betrayal: the woman he mourned was keeping the town's secrets alphabetized right alongside him.

chapters.title: The Visitor in the Grey Coat
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Flashback chapter: three weeks ago, a man arrived claiming to be Daniel Voss's brother, carrying proof that would expose the pact and drag Wren's name into a killing she didn't commit. Wren begged him to leave; he refused. She stole clothes from the stockroom to disguise him for a night escape — and someone else followed him to the mill. Beat: Wren's innocence established, her terror made concrete.

chapters.title: Hale Closes the Net
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Sergeant Hale arrests Wren on circumstantial evidence: her fingerprints on the grey coat, her lie about the visitor. Emrys knows she's covering for someone — or protecting him. Racing the trial clock, he cracks the ledger's final cipher and finds a payment scheduled for this week, signed with a symbol belonging to the churchwarden. Beat: urgency and protectiveness hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Confession at the Mill
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. At the ruined mill, Emrys traps the churchwarden, who admits he killed Voss's brother to bury the pact forever — and reveals the cruelest twist: Daniel Voss didn't abandon Wren; he left to gather evidence and died trying, and the families let everyone believe he ran. Beat: climax, physical and moral danger converging as Emrys records the confession while the mill begins to burn.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: POV Wren. With the churchwarden arrested, Wren waits for Emrys to hand over her own secret — the lies she told, the evidence she moved. Instead he sits across from her in the police station and tells Hale the truth about his own seven years of willful blindness, taking the weight of complicity onto himself. Beat: catharsis; duty fulfilled not by punishment but by truth-telling.

chapters.title: Alphabetized at Last
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Spring comes to Hollowmere. The founding families face consequences, the mill becomes a memorial garden, and Wren formally becomes Emrys's adopted daughter over tea in the bookshop. He files the last page of the ledger under 'F' — for finished — and shelves it beside Marian's photograph. Final beat: peace earned, found family sealed, secrets finally put in their proper place.
